summary: The rhythmic scheduling interval or pattern governing ticker executions and reactive signal updates.
details: Cadence can be fixed-interval (e.g. every 5 seconds via Ticker), cron/RRule-driven, or event-driven at unit-bucket boundaries via @tempo-kit/plugin-signals.

summary: A system for organizing days into months and years (such as iso8601, gregory, hebrew, or islamic-civil) tracked by every Tempo instance.
The gradual offset between local system time and true reference network time, compensated by the NTP plugin.
An external date/time format token grammar (such as LDML, Moment, POSIX strftime, or Oracle TO_CHAR) bridged by @tempo-kit/plugin-dialects.
An object implementing dispose() and Symbol.dispose for deterministic timer and subscription cleanup via TypeScript using declarations.
A signed span of calendar and clock units (years, months, days, hours, minutes, seconds, sub-seconds) used in Tempo arithmetic and formatting.
Tempo's pattern where configuration options (such as timeZone, locale, or calendar) accept lazy evaluator functions (() => T) resolved per request.
A Proxy-wrapped, null-prototype lookup dictionary built with Enum.from() or Enum.extend() that supports static reflection without prototype pollution.
Elapsed time since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z), exposed by Tempo as .epoch.ms (number) and .epoch.ns (bigint).
A canonical geographic region identifier (such as Australia/Sydney or America/New_York) carrying historical and DST offset rules.
A precise, absolute point on the universal temporal timeline, independent of time zones or calendars.
A half-open [start, end) span (inclusive start, exclusive end) between two temporal points supporting containment, overlap, union, and reactive state observation.
The international standard for date, time, UTC offset, duration, and week-date string representations.
Deferring expensive derived computations (such as calendar decompositions, formatted caches, and DFC options) until first read and memoizing the result.
A BCP 47 language tag (such as en-AU or fr-FR) governing month/weekday names, relative-time phrasing, numbering systems, and regional date parsing.
An orthogonal token extension (e.g., :compact, :hh, :ordinal, :roman, :zero) refining how a format token or term serializes or parses values.
A deeply frozen static or instance extension object mounted on Tempo via defineNamespace() or definePlugin() (e.g., Tempo.signals, t.geo).
A fixed numeric displacement from UTC (e.g., +10:00 or -05:00), distinct from an IANA time zone which carries historical and DST transition rules.
Tempo's layout selection and scoring subsystem that matches ambiguous input strings against registered snippets, dialects, and regional date layouts.
The two-digit year century cutoff (default 75) controlling whether 2-digit years resolve to 19xx or 20xx during parsing.
A calendar date (year, month, day) without reference to a specific time of day, time zone, or geographical location.
A wall-clock date and time without an attached time zone or UTC offset.
A reactive accessor function adhering to the TC39 Signals proposal (Signify) that notifies subscribers of value and epoch changes.
The Internet Extended Date/Time Format (IXDTF) standard extending RFC 3339 with bracketed time zone and calendar annotations (e.g., [Australia/Sydney][u-ca=iso8601]).

An isolated Tempo subclass created via Tempo.extend() with its own configuration and plugin isolation for multi-tenant SSR or testing (term access uses the shared runtime term map, so tenants registering different terms under the same key can conflict).
A named regular-expression fragment registered in the parsing engine to match recurring sub-patterns (such as dates, times, or ordinals).
Tempo's immutability strategy that provides non-destructive mutations without incurring the heavy V8 runtime cost of deep recursive Object.freeze().
A modular unit of temporal formatting, parsing, or range partitioning registered in the engine registry (e.g. #quarter, #season, #timeOfDay).
A bracketed lowercase format or parse placeholder inside a Tempo mask (e.g., {yyyy}, {mm}, {dd}, {hh}, {mi}, {ss}, {tz}).
A time-zone-aware, calendar-aware date and time combining an exact Instant, an IANA time zone, and a calendar system; Tempo's underlying Temporal representation.
